findings.finding: Fresh observation provenance is not bound per target row. The map has one top-level build_id, while each of seven target records has only observed=true and no row-specific build identity or digest/reference to the verifier observation/log. match_first_and_only_error accepts arbitrary caller log_text and does not establish that it came from the declared build. Thus the helper can validate seven self-consistent rows while failing its stated requirement that each be a fresh observed target.
findings.fix: Bind each target record to its own fresh observation identity (or to an explicit single-build matrix record that proves all seven variants), and bind the matched diagnostic input to that identity, e.g. with a content digest/reference and a validated receipt contract. Keep this as observation validation only; do not imply proof acceptance.

findings.finding: The no-retained-half anchor only requires one global occurrence of RETAINED_HALF_MERGE and one global occurrence of FULL_CELL_ASSERT, with the former byte offset earlier than the latter. It does not require either anchor to be inside the same select_unpredictable body or even the same function. A source containing the merge in one function and the full-cell assertion later in another can pass this anchor check and assign a diagnostic to the unrelated assertion line.
findings.fix: Anchor both snippets within one uniquely identified select_unpredictable body (and require the expected returned-guard context/order); fail closed if function boundaries or context are ambiguous.

nits: The helper is explicitly inactive and returns no acceptance or proof credit; this review does not treat it as an activated classifier or as evidence that any target was observed.

The caller-supplied source bytes, tool-spec bytes, and tool path are internally self-consistent but are not independently tied here to a physical file or pinned expected digest; keep the documented external source/stage binding mandatory at any future integration.
